title: JOBAN SINGH versus STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
UKHC010206912025
2026:UHC:8531
1
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition Service Single No. 2273 of 2025
22 September, 2026
Joban Singh and Another --Petitioners
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand and Others --Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Priyansh Mittal, learned counsel for petitioners.
Mr. D.S. Bankoti, learned Brief Holder for the State of
Uttarakhand/respondents.
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J. (Oral)
Delay in filing the counter affidavit is
condoned. Delay condonation application (IA/2/ 2026) is
allowed. Counter affidavit filed by the State is taken on
record.
2. By means of the present writ petition,
petitioners have sought the following reliefs:-
1. To issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
Certiorari, quashing the recovery order dated
17.05.2021 issued against petitioner No.1 and
recovery orders dated 04.06.2021 issued against
petitioner Nos.1 and 2 (Annexure No.3 and Annexure
No.4), which has been passed illegally, in light of the
law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in State
of Punjab Vs. Rafiq Masih [(2015) 4 SCC 334]
(Annexure No.6) as well as the guidelines of the
Department of Personnel & Training, Ministry of
Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions (Annexure
No.5).
2. To issue a writ, order or direction the nature of
Mandamus, directing the Respondents to release the
amounts of Rs.4,31,367 and Rs. 1,64,634 as illegally
recovered from Petitioner No.1 and Petitioner No.2
respectively (Annexure No.3 and Annexure No.4).
3. The brief facts of the case are that petitioners
were employed with Public Works Department,
Dehradun, as Helper (Class-IV employee) and

UKHC010206912025
2026:UHC:8531
2
Compressor Operator (Class-IV employee) respectively.
Both the petitioners were superannuated on 31.03.2021
upon attaining the age of superannuation. On1
17.05.2021, much after their retirement, respondent
No.3 issued recovery letter against petitioner No.1
claiming an amount of ₹2,79,873/- from his gratuity
amount, relying upon G.O. No.1197/III(1) 2019-09(3)
General/16 dated 14.08.2019, which provides for
recovery from employees for various reasons. Thereafter,
another recovery letter dated 04.06.2021 was issued by
respondent No.3 to petitioners, whereby, recovery of
₹4,31,367/- and ₹1,64,634/- were directed to be
recovered from gratuity of petitioner Nos.1 and 2
respectively, under clauses 1, 2 and 3 of the aforesaid
GO. Thus, petitioners are before this Court challenging
the aforesaid recovery orders.
4. Learned counsel for petitioners submits that
according to Department of Personnel and Training,
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions,
any recovery from employees belonging to Class-III and
Class-IV service (Group-C and Group-D service) is
impermissible in law, it also elaborated all the situations
in which the recoveries will be impermissible in law. For
support of said contention, he also annexed the letter of
Department of Personnel and Training as Annexure No.5
to the writ petition.
5. Learned counsel for petitioner relied upon para
12 of the judgment rendered by Hon'ble Apex Court in
the case of State of Punjab Versus Rafiq Masih,
reported in 2015 (4) SCC 334, wherein, it was held that
recovery from the class III and IV employees cannot be
made, if the employee did not receive the same by playing

UKHC010206912025
2026:UHC:8531
3
fraud and misrepresentation. For ready reference, Para
12 is reproduced below:
"12. It is not possible to postulate all situations of hardship,
which would govern employees on the issue of recovery,
where payments have mistakenly been made by the
employer, in excess of their entitlement. Be that as it may,
based on the decisions referred to herein above, we may, as a
ready reference, summarise the following few situations,
wherein recoveries by the employers, would be impermissible
in law:
(i) Recovery from employees belonging to Class-III and Class-IV service (or Group 'C' and Group 'D' service).
(ii) Recovery from retired employees, or employees who are
due to retire within one year, of the order of recovery.
(iii) Recovery from employees, when the excess payment has
been made for a period in excess of five years, before the
order of recovery is issued.
(iv) Recovery in cases where an employee has wrongfully been
required to discharge duties of a higher post, and has
been paid accordingly, even though he should have
rightfully been required to work against an inferior post.
(v) In any other case, where the Court arrives at the
conclusion, that recovery if made from the employee,
would be iniquitous or harsh or arbitrary to such an
extent, as would far outweigh the equitable balance of the
employer's right to recover."
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner further
submits that all the service benefits, whatsoever have
been granted to petitioners, have legally been granted to
them and otherwise also, assuming without admitting, if
they were granted the some benefits wrongly, even then,
as they did not receive the same by playing fraud and
misrepresentation, therefore the department cannot
make recovery of the same. The action of the
respondents, besides being illegal, unjust, arbitrary, is
also against the principles enunciated by the Hon'ble
Supreme Court.
7. Learned State Counsel however submits
that on implementation of the 6th Pay Commission,
the salary of petitioner No.1 was wrongly determined
and thus, excess payment of ₹2,48,733/- was paid to

UKHC010206912025
2026:UHC:8531
4
petitioner No.1 from 01.01.2006 till the date of
retirement i.e. 31.03.2021. After fixation of salary of
petitioner No.1, the last pay drawn at the time of
retirement of petitioner No.1 was determined at
₹33,300/-, while he was getting ₹37,500/- as salary
on retirement. Therefore, a total recovery of excess
payment No.2 amounting to ₹4,31,367/- was made
from petitioner No.1. Further, on implementation of
the 6th Pay Commission, the salary of petitioner was
wrongly determined and thus, excess payment of
₹1,38,894/- was paid to petitioner No.2 from
01.01.2006 to 31.03.2021 and also paid an amount
of ₹25,740/- in cash, therefore, totaling ₹1,64,634/-
excess payment was paid to petitioner No.2.
Therefore, a total recovery of excess payment
amounting to ₹1,64,634/- was made from petitioner
No.2.
8. Having heard the contentions of learned
counsel for the parties and having perused the material
available on record, this Court is of the view that the case
of the petitioners is squarely covered by the judgment of
Apex Court in the case of State of Punjab Versus Rafiq
Masih, reported in 2015 (4) SCC 334. In the said case, it
has been categorically held that if excess payment has
been made to Class III and IV employees and they were
not involved in any fraud or misrepresentation regarding
the same no recovery shall be made from them. In the
case in hand it is nobody's case that the petitioners were
involved in fraud or misrepresentation regarding the
excess payment and fixation of excess basic pay,
therefore, this writ petition is allowed.

UKHC010206912025
2026:UHC:8531
5
9. Accordingly, the impugned order dated
17.05.2021 issued against petitioner No.1 and recovery
orders dated 04.06.2021 issued against petitioners are
hereby quashed, to the extent of recovery of ₹4,31,367/-
and ₹1,64,634/-, and a writ of mandamus is issued
directing the respondents to repay the amount of
₹4,31,367/- and ₹1,64,634/-, which has been deducted
from their retiral dues without any fault of them,
therefore the amount recovered, shall be released in their
favour, along with interest @5% per annum from the date
of recovery till actual payment is made, within ten weeks
from the date of presentation of certified copy of this
order.
10. Pending application, if any, stands disposed of.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 22.09.2026
